record.title: A co-tenant Event can prevent release of another Project's closed Haunting group
record.description: When one daemon serves two granted Projects using the same service name, a Credential holder in Project B can submit a valid Event for that service (e.g. a warning 'http.request', a type unhandled by createRules, so no B detection is produced) while B has no active Haunting. The active lookup for B deletes the service-only byService cache entry belonging to Project A, but its attempted release is restricted to B and leaves A's watcher group intact. If A's durable Haunting is closed before its next eligible detection, that detection reuses the unreleased [A,service] group. The daemon loads A's closed record by ID, spreads prior.incident after change.incident so the closed state wins, and appends the new detection to that closed row rather than opening the fresh active Haunting expected by the existing single-Project close/reopen behavior (which the source test 'a persisted closed Haunting releases the old in-memory group for the next observation' exercises). The minimum claimed boundary result is a new Project A detection being recorded on a closed Haunting because of Project B's Event.
record.claimed_root_cause: createObservations stores active IDs in byService under service alone (lines 42, 50, 69, 92-97), whereas createGrouper stores open groups under [detection.projectId,detection.service] (pipeline.ts:44). Cache deletion, replacement and release therefore refer to different namespaces: B's null-active lookup deletes A's service-only cache ID while release(B,A-id) is refused by the grouper's Project equality check (pipeline.ts:79). Durable Project checks in HauntingRepo.upsert (haunting.repo.ts:28,47-57) protect row ownership and monotonic updates but do not repair the stale group, and haunting.mapper.mergeRecorded/hauntingData preserve the prior closed incident state on the appended detection.

trace.description: A Project B Credential with events:publish may publish an Event whose body.projectId is B and whose body.service is a shared service name such as 'checkout' (project/service binding is checked at lines 31-35). A warning 'http.request' Event is schema-valid but unhandled by createRules, so it exercises the daemon active lookup without creating a B detection.

The daemon is booted with boot.projectIds (main.ts:71) and passes them as grantedProjectIds; processQueued admits any granted Project and serially invokes the single createObservations runtime registered at main.ts:115-155.

For B, the project-scoped active lookup (lines 79-83) returns null. old = byService.get('checkout') is A's incident ID; watcher.release(B,A-id) is called at line 93 and line 94 deletes byService['checkout'], losing A's cache ID while A's group survives.
release compares entry.projectId with the caller's projectId (B) at line 79, so it refuses to delete A's [A,'checkout'] group. A's stale group remains open while its cache entry is gone.

After A's durable Haunting is resolved, A's next eligible detection finds the still-open [A,'checkout'] group via the key at line 44, so add() at lines 64-75 does not call newId() and returns an 'updated' change carrying the old A incident ID and stale 'open' state.

The get-by-ID call at lines 107-111 uses A's projectId and the reused old ID, returning A's closed row. The spread at lines 123-131 places ...change.incident before ...(prior?.incident ?? {}), so the closed prior state overrides the stale 'open' state while the new detection and updatedAt are retained.

The authoritative row lookup is scoped by (projectId=A, id=old A id) at line 47; matching service/openedAt and monotonic updatedAt checks at lines 51-57 pass, so the tx.haunting.upsert at lines 61-66 writes the closed row's state back with the appended detection. No new active Haunting is created for A's detection.

evidence.description: byService is Map<string,string> keyed by service alone; its reads/writes/deletes at lines 50, 69 and 92-97 carry no Project component.
Open groups are keyed by JSON.stringify([detection.projectId,detection.service]), so the watcher and bridge cache disagree about identity.
active() at lines 98-105 filters state notIn ['resolved','dismissed'] at line 100 and scopes by projectId, so A's later null response is legitimate but the missing service cache ID prevents release.
mergeRecorded takes the next incident state (lines 69-76) and hauntingData writes incident.state directly to the row (line 48); there is no closed-to-new-detection lifecycle rejection.
The checks at lines 84-91 validate the returned active service, state and detection Project, but they do not scope byService itself, which remains service-only.
The single-Project test 'a persisted closed Haunting releases the old in-memory group for the next observation' confirms the intended close/reopen baseline that the cross-Project sequence breaks.

blockers: The two-Project lifecycle sequence has not been observed: source-only review is required and complete OS-enforced memory, cumulative-disk, filesystem and wall-clock sandbox controls are unavailable, so target-code execution, tests and fixture processing are forbidden. Source establishes the deterministic logic but not the observed durable boundary result (which row/state the final write produces and that no fresh active Haunting is created).

validation_plan.local: Once a parent-approved sandbox with no external network, empty allowlisted environment, read-only target, scratch-only writes and explicit low memory/disk/CPU/wall-clock limits is available, build one createObservations instance with a fake PrivateApi whose haunting records are keyed by (projectId,id) and whose active() is project-scoped and excludes resolved/dismissed rows. Seed A's open Haunting for service 'checkout' via an A runtime.oom Event. Deliver a distinct B Event for 'checkout' with a type unhandled by createRules (e.g. 'http.request', severity 'warning') while B has no active Haunting; confirm byService['checkout'] is deleted, A's group is still present, and no B write occurs. Mark A's stored row resolved in the fixture (no daemon Event). After the ten-minute dedupe window (watcher/types.ts:59), deliver a fresh A runtime.oom Event and inspect the next write payload, its incident id/state and the active lookup: correct behavior opens a new active Haunting with a fresh incident id; the predicted defect appends A's detection to the closed A-id row with state 'resolved'. Mock the gateway and Work port so no model call or paid action occurs. Stop at this observation; no deployed or shared service is contacted.
